mainTopic: שמואל's rule linking חטאת and פסח, whether חצות or שחיטה decides when a lost פסח becomes a שלמים, and a new משנה on an animal unfit to be a פסח.
overview: The גמרא is trying to fit שמואל's two-part rule into a known opinion. The rule says that where a חטאת dies, a פסח is brought as a שלמים, and where a חטאת grazes, a פסח grazes. Following רבי, it finds a grazing חטאת in רבי אושעיא's backup case, but in that same case a פסח becomes a שלמים, so the parallel breaks. It then says שמואל follows רבי שמעון, for whom these חטאות always die, and explains that שמואל really stated only one rule: whatever makes a חטאת die makes a פסח into a שלמים. שמואל's new point is to argue with רבי יוחנן: for שמואל, חצות, not the slaughter of the replacement, decides whether a lost פסח counts as pushed aside. A second version runs the discussion differently. It first tries to say שמואל holds like רבה (the slaughter decides), rejects that because of רבי יוחנן's dispute, and concludes that שמואל holds like רבי, with חצות as the deciding moment. The amud ends with a new משנה: an animal that could never be a valid פסח, such as a female or a two-year-old male, grazes until blemished, is sold, and its money buys a voluntary שלמים.

steps.title: A case of a grazing sin-offering, from Rabbi Oshaya
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is a case where a חטאת is left to graze: when someone set aside two חטאות as backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי אושעיא, who said: if someone set aside two sin-offerings as a backup, he gets atonement with one, and the second is left to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question just raised on the previous amud. Even according to רבי, who holds that a lost חטאת goes to die, there is a case where a חטאת is left to graze (רועה): the case of רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone sets aside two animals for one חטאת, on purpose, so that one serves as backup (לאחריות). Once he brings one, the extra one is not killed. It is left to graze until it gets a blemish. This supplies a real example of a 'grazing' חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside (designated an animal as a קרבן)
As a guarantee or backup, in case one is lost
It is left to graze until it gets a blemish, then it is sold

steps.confusionAlert: 'Grazing' (רועה) does not mean the animal lives forever in the field. It means it grazes until it gets a blemish, and then it is sold and the money is used for a voluntary קרבן. 'Dying' (מתה) means it is locked away until it dies.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Oshaya.
For Rabbi Oshaya said:
If one separated two sin-offerings as a guarantee —
he gains atonement with one of them,
and the second is left to graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud about whether there is any case of a grazing חטאת under the view being considered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי's view, that a lost חטאת goes to die, there might be no case of a חטאת that grazes at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is such a case: the backup חטאת of רבי אושעיא.

steps.title: In the same case, a Paschal lamb becomes a peace-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in רבי אושעיא's case, a פסח would be offered as a שלמים, which does not fit שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if this were a פסח, in a case like this it would be offered as a peace-offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. In the backup case, a פסח would be brought as a שלמים, and that does not match the way שמואל's rule was being read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's statement, as quoted on the previous amud, had a second half: whatever makes a חטאת graze makes a פסח graze too. In רבי אושעיא's backup case the extra חטאת grazes, but the extra פסח in the same case is offered as a שלמים, not left to graze. So explaining שמואל according to רבי fails as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is offered as a peace-offering

phrases.english: But if it were a Paschal lamb,
in a case like this it is offered as a peace-offering!

steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to explain שמואל through רבי אושעיא's case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבי אושעיא's case the backup חטאת grazes, but a backup פסח is offered as a שלמים. This contradicts the 'where a חטאת grazes, a פסח grazes' side of שמואל's parallel.

steps.title: שמואל holds like רבי שמעון: five sin-offerings die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes approach: שמואל follows רבי שמעון, who holds that all five problem חטאות are left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, who said: five sin-offerings are left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier approach. It now says שמואל agrees with רבי שמעון, who rules that all five kinds of disqualified חטאת die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals a fresh start. רבי שמעון has a simple rule with no 'grazing' category for these cases: lost or pushed-aside חטאות are left to die. Matching שמואל to this clean view is meant to avoid the earlier mismatches.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous approach and offers a new one
Five kinds of sin-offering that are left to die

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rather, Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who said: five sin-offerings are left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by switching which תנא שמואל follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the view to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל follows a view that includes a 'grazing' case such as רבי אושעיא's.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון: these חטאות die.

steps.title: רבי שמעון has no grazing category at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי שמעון never has a חטאת that grazes, yet שמואל's statement talked about grazing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון does not hold of 'grazing' at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new approach. רבי שמעון has no case of a grazing חטאת, so how could שמואל, who seemed to mention grazing, follow him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי שמעון, every pushed-aside חטאת dies. Any part of שמואל's statement that relied on a 'grazing' חטאת would have nothing to refer to. So the match with רבי שמעון seems to break.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it (does not accept it)

phrases.english: But 'grazing,' according to Rabbi Shimon,
he does not hold of at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רוֹעָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ כְּלָל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's statement seemed to include a 'grazing חטאת' rule, and רבי שמעון has no such category.

steps.title: שמואל stated only one rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל really said only one rule: whatever makes a חטאת die makes a פסח into a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל, too, said only one rule: anything that would make a sin-offering die, in a Paschal lamb it is offered as a peace-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by rereading שמואל. He never mentioned a grazing חטאת. He said only one thing: wherever a חטאת would die, a פסח is offered as a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By cutting שמואל's statement down to a single rule, the clash with רבי שמעון disappears. Now the rule fits רבי שמעון perfectly: in every case where his חטאת dies, the matching פסח becomes a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that, in a sin-offering, dies

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of שמואל's rule, following רבי שמעון: כל שבחטאת מתה, בפסח קרב שלמים. Whatever would make a חטאת die makes a פסח into a שלמים.

phrases.english: Shmuel, too, said only one rule:
Anything that, in a sin-offering, dies —
in a Paschal lamb, it is offered as a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the wording of שמואל's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל made a two-part statement that included a grazing חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל made only one statement: חטאת מתה, so פסח is קרב שלמים.

steps.title: What new point is שמואל teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל adds, since the משנה already shows that a pushed-aside פסח becomes a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does he teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that שמואל's rule is settled, the גמרא asks what is new in it. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule only repeats what the משנה already says, there is no reason for שמואל to state it. The גמרא assumes that an אמורא's statement must add something, so it looks for the hidden new point.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he teach us (that is new)?

phrases.english: And what does he teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the settled rule and asks what it adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point שמואל's rule adds beyond the משנה

steps.title: Excluding רבי יוחנן's view about the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: שמואל comes to reject רבי יוחנן, who says a פסח becomes a שלמים only if it is found after the replacement was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude רבי יוחנן, who said: a פסח is offered as a peace-offering only if it was found after the slaughter, but before the slaughter, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל is arguing against רבי יוחנן. For רבי יוחנן, a lost פסח becomes a שלמים only if it was found after the other animal was already slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, if the lost פסח turns up before the replacement is slaughtered, it does not become a שלמים. The moment of שחיטה is what matters for him. שמואל's rule is aimed at this view.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Yochanan,
who said: the Paschal lamb is not offered as a peace-offering
unless it was found after the slaughter,
but before the slaughter — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what שמואל adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל is arguing against רבי יוחנן's view that a פסח becomes a שלמים only if found after the slaughter.

steps.title: Midday, not slaughter, is the deciding moment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the slaughter is the deciding moment. שמואל teaches that midday (חצות) is.
steps.simpleTranslation: So for רבי יוחנן, the slaughter determines. שמואל teaches us: midday determines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the dispute. For רבי יוחנן the slaughter fixes the status, while שמואל says חצות on ערב פסח fixes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חצות is when the time to slaughter the פסח begins. For שמואל, if the פסח is still lost at חצות, it is already considered pushed aside, so when found it is offered as a שלמים, even if the replacement was not yet slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: Midday of ערב פסח, when the time for slaughtering the פסח begins

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute in one line: רבי יוחנן says שחיטה קבע (the slaughter decides), שמואל says חצות קבע (midday decides) whether a lost פסח found later becomes a שלמים.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'slaughter' here means the slaughter of the replacement פסח, not of the lost one. The question is whether the lost animal was found before or after its replacement was slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the exact moment when a lost פסח loses its status as a פסח and is brought as a שלמים instead.

phrases.english: Apparently: the slaughter determines.
He teaches us: midday determines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the principle behind רבי יוחנן's view and states שמואל's opposing principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל: חצות decides whether a פסח is pushed aside, so if it is still lost at midday, it is offered as a שלמים when found.

steps.title: Second version: a lost פסח found before the slaughter seems to break שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the גמרא challenges שמואל's rule with a פסח that was lost and found after חצות but before the replacement was slaughtered. That פסח is offered as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: But in the case of a פסח that was lost and then found after midday, before the slaughter, it should be offered as a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the discussion. It opens with a challenge to שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule pairs the two offerings: where a חטאת dies, a פסח becomes a שלמים, and where a חטאת grazes, a פסח grazes. Here a פסח found after חצות but before the replacement was slaughtered becomes a שלמים. The matching חטאת case is one found before the owner gains atonement with its replacement, and there (according to the חכמים) the חטאת grazes and is not sent to die. So the two do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same discussion
Midday, when the time for slaughtering the פסח begins

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is telling the same back-and-forth over again, the way a different tradition remembered it.

phrases.english: Another version:
But with a Paschal lamb, where it was lost
and was found after midday,
before the slaughter, it is offered as a peace-offering!
phrases.notes: This means before the replacement פסח was slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: וְאִילּוּ בְּפֶסַח הֵיכָא דְּאָבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the analysis of שמואל's rule as a second version.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that whatever makes a חטאת die makes a פסח into a שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here a פסח becomes a שלמים in a case where the matching חטאת would not clearly die. So the parallel breaks.

steps.title: שמואל holds like רבה: the slaughter decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל agrees with רבה, who says the slaughter of the replacement is the deciding moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבה, who said: the slaughter determines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying שמואל agrees with רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slaughter is the deciding moment, a פסח found before the slaughter does not count as lost at all. So שמואל would not make it a שלמים, and his rule still matches the חטאת case.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds like Rabba,
who said: the slaughter determines.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns שמואל to a known opinion (רבה) that removes the problem case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסח found after חצות counts as lost, so it becomes a שלמים even though the חטאת would not die.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the slaughter decides. Before the slaughter the פסח is not lost, so the case never comes up.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's argument shows שמואל holds that חצות decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. רבי יוחנן argued with שמואל by saying the slaughter decides. So שמואל must hold that חצות decides, not the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since רבי יוחנן said about this: a פסח is offered as a שלמים only if it was found after the slaughter, but not before the slaughter — clearly he holds the slaughter determines. That implies שמואל holds midday determines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said about שמואל's rule (עלה) that a פסח becomes a שלמים only if it was found after the slaughter, so for him the slaughter decides. His statement only makes sense as a disagreement with שמואל, so שמואל must hold the other side: חצות decides. That means שמואל cannot agree with רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he said

phrases.english: But from the fact that Rabbi Yochanan said about it:
The Paschal lamb is not offered as a peace-offering
unless it was found after the slaughter,
but before the slaughter — no.
Clearly: the slaughter determines.
This implies that Shmuel holds: midday determines.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל holds like רבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן argued with שמואל by saying the slaughter decides. So שמואל must hold that חצות decides.

steps.title: Instead, שמואל holds like רבי: a lost חטאת goes to die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. שמואל agrees with רבי, who says any lost חטאת is sent to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: שמואל holds like רבי, who said: a lost animal goes to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the רבה answer and offers a new one: שמואל follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, a lost חטאת always dies, even if it is found before the owner gains atonement through a replacement. So the פסח found after חצות matches a חטאת that dies, and שמואל's rule works.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost (חטאת) goes to its death
Rather; introduces a new answer after the old one failed

phrases.english: Rather: Shmuel holds like Rabbi,
who said: a lost animal goes to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed answer of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns שמואל to a different תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל holds like רבה, that the slaughter decides.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds like רבי: every lost חטאת dies, so the פסח found after חצות matches.

steps.title: For רבי every lost animal dies, yet a פסח lost and found before חצות just grazes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. For רבי, all lost חטאות die. But a פסח lost and found before חצות does not become a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבי all lost animals die, whereas a פסח lost before midday and found before midday grazes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל matches the פסח to רבי's rule, then any lost פסח should become a שלמים. Yet a פסח lost and found before חצות does not become a שלמים. So the match seems to break again.

keyTerms.meaning: Grazes; is left in the field and not sacrificed as a שלמים

phrases.english: But for Rabbi, all lost animals die,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ בְּפֶסַח, הֵיכָא דְּאָבַד קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת
phrases.english: whereas with a Paschal lamb, where it was lost before midday
and found before midday — it grazes!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל holds like רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי, any loss leads to death. But a פסח lost and found before חצות does not become a שלמים, so the parallel fails.

steps.title: Before חצות a פסח does not count as lost, and חצות decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פסח missing before חצות is not considered lost, because its time has not yet come. חצות is the deciding moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: before midday it is not considered lost. And he holds midday determines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and closes the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח can only be slaughtered from חצות on. So if it goes missing and turns up before חצות, nothing was missed, and it never counts as lost. The status is set at חצות, which fits what step 11 showed: שמואל holds that חצות decides.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, שמואל holds like רבי: a lost חטאת always dies. For a פסח, "lost" only counts from חצות, because חצות is the deciding moment, not the slaughter.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת לָאו אָבוּד הוּא,
phrases.english: He holds: before midday it is not considered lost,
and he holds midday determines.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת לָאו אָבוּד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and ends the second version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines when "lost" begins for a פסח
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסח missing before חצות counts as lost, so by רבי's rule it should become a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before חצות it is not lost at all. Loss is measured at חצות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל holds like רבי, with חצות as the deciding moment.

steps.title: משנה: a female or two-year-old male set aside as a פסח
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules on an animal that cannot be a valid פסח. It grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold, and the money buys a voluntary שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sets aside a female for his פסח, or a male in its second year — it grazes until it becomes blemished, then it is sold, and its money goes to voluntary offerings, for שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with someone who set aside an animal that could never be a valid פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח must be a male in its first year, so a female or a two-year-old male can never be offered as one. Since it is still holy, it cannot simply be used. Instead it waits for a blemish, is sold, and the money is used for a voluntary שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside (an animal for an offering)
Until it becomes blemished and unfit

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming discussion of what happens to an animal set aside for a פסח that was never fit to be one.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sets aside a female for his Paschal lamb,
or a male in its second year —
it grazes until it becomes blemished,
and it is sold, and its money goes
to voluntary offerings, for peace-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal that is unfit to be a פסח grazes until blemished, then is sold, and the money buys a voluntary שלמים.
